clips.text_en_b1: HAPPENING — OIL $150 IS ABOUT TO BE REALITY BROS. Jim Cramer posted on X that crude could hit $150 soon. Anons are split: some say it's hopium, others point to real supply risk in the Middle East. Either way, oil is already ripping this week and energy stocks are green again.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread quoting Jim Cramer on $150 oil

signal.rationale: OP cites Cramer's $150 oil call amid Middle East tension; energy/oil thesis implies hard-asset hedge via gold

clips.text_en_b2: BREAKING: OIL COULD HIT $150 AND NOBODY'S PAYING ATTENTION. Jim Cramer dropped a post on X suggesting crude is heading towards $150, and /biz/ is absolutely losing it. While some anons are brushing it off as hopium, others point to genuine supply-side risk brewing in the Middle East. Although Cramer's track record is pretty hit-or-miss, WTI is already ripping this week and energy stocks are firmly back in the green.
clips.text_en_c1: The prospect of crude oil breaching $150 is once again doing the rounds, with Jim Cramer publicly suggesting on X that the benchmark could approach that level sooner than markets anticipate. While seasoned traders remain sceptical — pointing out that his calls have historically been anything but reliable — there is a grudging acknowledgment that Middle Eastern supply disruptions could lend the thesis some traction. WTI has already been climbing throughout the week, and energy equities are firmly back in positive territory, regardless of whether the prognosticator ultimately proves correct.
clips.text_en_c2: Jim Cramer has once again taken to X to proclaim that crude is destined for $150, a forecast that, given his track record of conspicuous misfires, would normally be dismissed outright. Yet this time the Middle East situation appears genuinely combustible, with WTI already posting a meaningful rally this week and energy names greening across the board. Anons remain divided: the permabears sniff hopium and point to decades of failed calls, while others note that supply disruption is no longer a theoretical risk but an observable reality. For those tempted to reload longs, the tuition costs have historically been punitive. Proceed with the caveat that every prior Cramer breakout prediction has eventually met the same ignominious end.

clips.text_en_b2: DOGE TO FUCKING SPACE IN THREE DAYS. Look, if this thing genuinely explodes it's still going to rip higher first, so why not throw a small position at it and take profits before it turns into SNL 2.0? That said, posts like these show up every single cycle, and nine times out of ten they end in tears. Whether we're witnessing the start of a fresh hype cycle or another classic pump-and-dump remains to be seen, but the board is completely split.
clips.text_en_c1: The familiar refrain that Dogecoin is destined for the stratosphere within seventy-two hours has resurfaced once more on /biz/, and reactions remain characteristically divided. Veteran anons will recognise the pattern: an initial pump, a euphoric chorus of true believers, followed inevitably by a brutal retrace that punishes the latecomers. Yet if the asset were to break out convincingly, even a modest position could yield returns before the inevitable SNL 2.0 dénouement. Whether this constitutes a genuine paradigm shift or merely the latest instalment of cyclical meme-coin theatrics remains, as ever, anyone's guess.
clips.text_en_c2: The familiar refrain returns: Dogecoin shall ascend to improbable stratospheric valuations within seventy-two hours, and the perpetually incredulous are urged to position accordingly. The reflexive response, conditioned by countless prior pump-and-dump cycles terminating in tears, is to scoff and move on. And yet, as several anons note with no small measure of irony, even a failed breakout typically produces enough upward momentum to reward a modest speculative position, provided one exits before the post-Nasdaq-listing SNL-style collapse. Others argue the broader meme-coin narrative is already morphing into its next iteration regardless. The board is predictably fractured between loaders gleefully apeing in and skeptics howling at what they perceive as terminal cope. Either way, three days.

clips.text_en_b1: Stuck with a Condo. In 2021 when I was 22 I made a bunch of random crypto money from dogecoin. Lived for two years with no job, perma vacation, dropped out of school and bought a condo for $230K. Eventually the money ran out. Went back to school, graduated, and now make $100K living in my condo.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ condo regret story tied to 2021 dogecoin

signal.rationale: No trading setup, lifestyle/finance observation post

clips.text_en_b2: Stuck with a Condo at 27. Back in 2021 I struck it lucky on some random dogecoin gamble at 22, quit school, and blew two years travelling while spending absolutely nothing on rent. With the profits I put a down payment on a $230K condo, which felt like winning the lottery at the time. Eventually the money dried up, I went back to school, graduated, and now I'm pulling $100K a year living in the place I once considered a trophy.
clips.text_en_c1: Having stumbled into modest crypto wealth courtesy of Dogecoin in 2021, I committed the cardinal sin of mistaking luck for acumen. At twenty-two I abandoned my studies, embarked on an extended period of unemployed leisure, and purchased a condominium for $230,000. Predictably, the capital evaporated; I subsequently returned to university, graduated, and now earn approximately $100,000 annually while servicing both student loans and lingering credit-card debt. At twenty-seven, I find myself locked into an inescapable loop of labour, consumption, and the inevitable mortgage payment, with no obvious exit strategy.
clips.text_en_c2: The archetypal /biz/ cautionary tale unfolds: aged twenty-two in 2021, the poster stumbled into a windfall of indeterminate provenance via Dogecoin, whereupon he proceeded to abandon his studies, embark upon a two-year perma-vacation, and commit to a condominium purchase valued at $230K. The inevitability of arithmetic eventually reasserted itself when the funds evaporated. Now twenty-seven and gainfully employed at a $100K salary, he finds himself marooned within his own asset, burdened simultaneously by student loans and revolving credit obligations, trapped in the Sisyphean cycle of work, consume, repeat. The condo, once emblematic of liberated living, has calcified into a gilded cage whose mortgage payments constitute a monthly confession of premature financial exuberance.

clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin vs Gold. If you had to hold only one for the next 10 years, would you choose Bitcoin or gold? What makes your choice better than the other? Anons are arguing scarcity, halving cycles, central bank buying, ETF flows, and store-of-value theory. Classic /biz/ thread, no real answer.

signal.rationale: Long-term philosophical debate, no actionable trade

clips.text_en_b2: BITCOIN VS GOLD: THE TEN-YEAR GRUDGE MATCH. If you had to lock up capital in only one of these for the next decade, which would actually come out on top? Anons are throwing around scarcity arguments, halving cycles, central bank accumulation, ETF flows, and the usual store-of-value debate. Bitcoin clearly offers higher multiples, although that volatility cuts both ways, while gold tends to creep up reliably without ever truly mooning.
clips.text_en_c1: The perennial /biz/ question resurfaces: should one commit to a decade-long position in Bitcoin or in physical gold? Proponents of the former emphasise programmed scarcity, the quadrennial halving cycle, persistent ETF inflows, and the asymmetric upside inherent in a still-emerging asset class. Defenders of the latter counter that centuries of monetary history confer an unmatched store-of-value pedigree, free from the existential risks of regulatory backlash or technological obsolescence. No consensus emerges, predictably, though the thread offers a useful synthesis of competing narratives for those willing to read between the lines.
clips.text_en_c2: The perennial /biz/ theological dispute resurfaces in its classic formulation: over a ten-year horizon, the rational allocator must choose between Bitcoin and gold, and defend the selection with doctrinal rigour. The faithful on each side marshal their customary eschatology. BTC partisans invoke programmed scarcity, the quadrennial halving, and ETF-amplified demand flows that render gold's millennia-old store-of-value narrative quaint. Gold advocates counter with sovereign accumulation trends and the inconvenient observation that no central bank balance sheet currently denominates anything in satoshis. The debate, as ever, devolves into an unsolvable syllogism whose only genuine conclusion is that a diversified position obviates the need for resolution. Classic /biz/ territory, wherein consensus signals only that the thread has exhausted itself.

clips.text_en_b2: ANTHROPIC RESEARCHER WALKS OUT OVER 'OUT OF CONTROL' AI FEARS. Jacob Coxon, who has spent years training new models by feeding them colossal datasets, announced on Tuesday that he's done with the company. His reason is straightforward enough: he refuses to be part of the industry's headlong rush towards building AI systems capable of upgrading themselves. He worries that once a model can iteratively rewrite its own weights, the whole thing could spiral well beyond anyone's ability to contain.
clips.text_en_c1: A researcher at Anthropic has tendered his resignation over what he characterises as runaway, uncontrollable artificial intelligence. Jacob Coxon, whose remit involves training nascent models on colossal corpora of data, announced on Tuesday that he could no longer in good conscience participate in what he regards as a frenzied, industry-wide race towards self-improving systems. His specific concern is that recursively autonomous agents, once unleashed, could depart irreversibly from human oversight and precipitate catastrophic, potentially civilisation-ending consequences — a sobering caution from someone intimately acquainted with the underlying engineering.
clips.text_en_c2: Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon has tendered his resignation, citing profound disquiet over the industry's pell-mell pursuit of self-improving artificial intelligence. As someone professionally tasked with training successive model generations by ingesting vast corpora of data, Coxon occupies an unusually informed vantage point from which to observe the trajectory. His stated concern is not the familiar caricature of sci-fi apocalypse, but rather the sober possibility that recursive self-enhancement, once initiated beyond a certain threshold of capability, may prove catastrophically difficult to constrain. His departure crystallises a paradox now haunting the sector: those best positioned to perceive the risks are precisely those whose labour sustains the accelerating capability curve. The engineer, comfortable in routine, contemplates an unsettling horizon.

clips.text_en_b2: CHINA CRACKS 2NM WITHOUT EUV AND /POL/ IS LOSING ITS MIND. Anons are popping champagne, declaring the West finished and ASML basically dead money overnight. Pushback is mounting, though, with plenty pointing out that a single demo chip means little if yields are trash and mass production is still years out. TSMC itself hasn't even committed to 2nm volume manufacturing yet, so let's pump the brakes before we crown anyone.
clips.text_en_c1: Reports that Chinese semiconductor fabricators have demonstrated functional 2-nanometre chips without recourse to ASML's extreme-ultraviolet lithography platforms have sent ripples through the industry. On /pol/, the consensus among posters is that Western supremacy is effectively over and that ASML's equity is doomed; this assessment is, predictably, rather reductive. Practitioners in the field recognise that a single prototype bears little resemblance to high-yield mass production, a distinction TSMC itself has yet to resolve at the 2nm node. The implications for Hong Kong's semiconductor ecosystem, while potentially profound, remain to be substantiated by sustained commercial output.
clips.text_en_c2: Reports emanating from Chinese semiconductor laboratories suggest that sub-2nm-class nodes have been demonstrated without recourse to ASML's extreme ultraviolet lithography, an achievement that, if independently verified, would constitute a genuine inflection point in the technology contest. /pol/ predictably erupts, with some posters declaring the West strategically obsolete and ASML a corpse in waiting. More measured voices counter that a singular proof-of-concept, however photogenic, is worlds apart from sustained high-yield mass production, a distinction TSMC itself has yet to publicly demonstrate at this node. The geopolitical ramifications, particularly for downstream industries in Hong Kong and the broader region, remain contingent upon manufacturing maturity rather than headline-grabbing technical disclosures. Observers are advised to maintain epistemic humility.

clips.text_zh: 83kg fat → cut 到 65kg skinnyfat → 80kg 重新 bulk。🏋️ 卧推 1 plate，深蹲 90kg，硬拉 120kg。同我而家好似。但未夠肥仔信嗰個 level。lol
clips.text_en_b1: How do I know when I've bulked enough to cut and escape skinnyfat? In May 2025 I was 83kg fat, almost no muscle. I cut aggressively until mid-April 2026 and got down to 65kg skinnyfat, struggling to bench even the 20kg bar. Then I lean bulked up till now, back to 80kg.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ bulk-cut cycle thread with specific lift numbers
clips.text_en_b2: How do I actually know when I've bulked enough to cut and finally escape skinnyfat? Back in May 2025 I was a soft 83kg with virtually no muscle underneath, so I cut aggressively until mid-April 2026 and bottomed out at 65kg, where I could barely bench the empty 20kg bar. Since then I've been lean bulking and I'm back up to 80kg. My numbers have climbed with me: flat bench 3x8 at one plate, squat 3x6 at 90kg, and deadlift 3x8 at 120kg.
clips.text_en_c1: The perpetual dilemma of the recovering skinnyfat trainee is determining precisely when caloric surplus has done sufficient work to justify another cut. By May 2025 I was a bloated eighty-three kilograms with negligible musculature; an aggressive deficit brought me, by April 2026, to a gaunt sixty-five — at which point even the unladened twenty-kilogram barbell felt insurmountable on the bench. A subsequent lean bulk has restored me to eighty kilograms, and my working numbers have improved markedly: flat bench three by eight at one plate, squat three by six at ninety, and deadlift three by eight at one-twenty.
clips.text_en_c2: The eternal skinnyfat quandary presents itself once more, as the poster seeks empirical guidance on when surplus accumulation ought to terminate in favour of a cutting phase. His trajectory is instructively dramatic: from a substantially overweight eighty-three kilograms in May 2025, virtually devoid of meaningful muscle tissue, he subjected himself to an aggressive caloric deficit until mid-April 2026, emerging at a gaunt sixty-five kilograms and struggling to press even the unweighted twenty-kilogram bar. Subsequent lean bulking has restored him to eighty kilograms, whereupon his current working weights stand at a one-plate bench for three sets of eight, a ninety-kilogram squat for triples of six, and a one-hundred-twenty-kilogram deadlift. The metrics, while respectable, evidently remain insufficient to dispel lingering dysmorphia.

clips.text_en_c2: During a characteristically meandering late-night broadcast, mangaka Ishiguro indulged in the time-honoured creative prerogative of ranking his own creations, even rendering them in swimsuits for the audience's evident delectation. The conspicuous absence of Kon-senpai proper was partially mitigated by the inclusion of her super-deformed counterpart from the spin-off gag manga, a concession that satisfied few. The stream drifted amiably into nostalgia, Fire Emblem reminiscences, and the perpetually unresolved question of when Gundam 00's second season might materialise. Par for the comfortable /a/ course.
